question: If X ~ N(5, 16), then the first quartile of X is equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is **2.3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Understanding the Normal Distribution:**

 
 
• The notation X ~ N(5, 16) represents a normal distribution with a mean (μ) of 5 and a variance (σ²) of 16. The standard deviation (σ) is the square root of the variance, which is 4 in this case.
 
 
 
• **Calculating the First Quartile (Q1):**
 
 
• The first quartile (Q1) is the value below which 25% of the data falls. For a normal distribution, this corresponds to the 25th percentile.
 
• Using standard normal distribution tables or Z-scores, the Z-score for the 25th percentile is approximately -0.675.
 
• The formula to convert a Z-score to a value in a normal distribution is X = μ + Zσ.
 
• Substituting the values, we get Q1 = 5 + (-0.675) * 4 = 2.3.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (5.3):**

 
 
• 5.3 is incorrect as it is greater than the mean (5), and the first quartile should be less than the mean in a normal distribution.
 
 
 
• **Option 3 (4.3):**
 
 
• 4.3 is closer but still incorrect as it does not account for the correct Z-score for the 25th percentile.
 
 
 
• **Option 4 (3.3):**
 
 
• 3.3 is incorrect since it is further from the correct value of 2.3 when applying the Z-score method.
